title: The extensible no-$(k(n)+1)$-in-line problem
summary: The classical no-$k$-in-line problem asks for the largest number of points that can be placed on an $n \times n$ grid without having $k$ of them collinear. A natural extension, motivated by the analogous question by Erde for $k\in \mathbb{Z}$, is the \emph{extensible no-$(k(n)+1)$-in-line problem}, which seeks a subset of points in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with maximal possible density such that at most $k(n)$ points are collinear within the subgrid $[1,n]^2$.
